ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
DECEMBER 1999
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in December increased $8.4 billion or 4.1 percent to
$212.9 billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 1.0 percent November
increase. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 0.7 percent. New orders for 1999 are 7.3 percent above 1998.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $7.3 billion or 16.2 percent to $52.3 billion; all component industries
increased, led by aircraft and parts. This is the largest increase since August 1998. Electronic and other electrical
equipment, up six of the last seven months, increased $1.8 billion or 4.6 percent to $41.1 billion. Industrial machinery and
equipment, down six of the last eight months, decreased $1.7 billion or 4.2 percent to $37.4 billion. Primary metals, down
four of the last five months, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.5 percent to $15.3 billion.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in December increased $1.4 billion or 0.7 percent to $205.7 billion, following
a 1.0 percent November increase. This is the seventh increase in the last eight months. Shipments for 1999 are 6.0 percent
above 1998.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $1.3 billion or 2.7 percent to $49.6 billion; all component industries
increased, led by motor vehicles and parts. Electronic and other electrical cguipment increased $0.3 billion or 0.8 percent to
$35.9 billion. Primary metals, up seven of the last eight months, increased $0.1 billion or 0.6 percent to $15.6 billion.
Industrial machinery and equipment, down four of the last five months, decreased $0.6 billion or 1.6 percent to $38.3
billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in December increased $7.3 billion or 1.5 percent to $508.0
billion, following a 0.1 percent increase in November. This is the sixth consecutive monthly increase and the largest since
January. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up thirteen consecutive months, had the largest increase, $5.3 billion or
6.6 percent to $85.5 billion. Transportation equipment, up for the first time since January, increased $2.7 billion or 1.2
percent to $224.8 billion. Industrial machinery and equis})ment, down for the first time since June, decreased $0.9 billion or
1.1 percent to $80.3 billion. Primary metals decreased $0.4 billion or 1.1 percent to $32.0 billion. This is the largest
decrease since January.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in December increased $1.5 billion or 24.5 percent to $7.5
billion. Shipments decreased $0.8 billion or 11.3 percent to $6.3 billion. This is the largest decrease since December 1997.
Unfilled orders increased $1.1 billion or 1.2 percent to $92.5 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in December increased $4.7 billion or 8.6 percent to
$59.0 billion. This is the largest increase since January. Shipments increased $0.8 billion or 1.5 percent to $55.9 billion.
Unfilled orders increased $3.1 billion or 1.2 percent to $254.2 billion.
This is the largest increase since January. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders increased $1.5 billion or 3.2 percent to
$49.9 billion; shipments, down four of the last five months, decreased 0.1 percent to $47.7 billion; and unfilled orders, up
four consecutive months, increased $2.2 billion or 2.0 percent to $114.8 billion.
e REVISED NOVEMBER DATA Revised seasonally adjusted November figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $364.9 billion (revised from $364.5 billion); new orders, $365.5 billion (revised from $365.2 billion); unfilled
orders, $526.5 billion (revised from $526.6 billion); and total inventories, $469.5 billion (revised from $469.7 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
April 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)

e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in April decreased $14.1 billion or 6.4 percent to $205.6
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 4.5 percent March increase and
is the largest decrease since December 1991. Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 6.4 percent. Year-to-date,
new orders are 7.6 percent above the same period a year ago.
Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest decrease, $9.0 billion or 20.1 percent to $35.7 billion, mostly due
to electronic components. This is the largest decrease on record. Transportation equipment decreased $3.2 billion or 6.7
percent to $45.5 billion; all components decreased, led by motor vehicles and parts. Primary metals decreased $0.3 billion
or 2.1 percent to $15.5 billion. This is the largest decrease since January 1999. Industrial machinery and equipment
increased $0.9 billion or 2.2 percent to $43.2 billion.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in April decreased $1.6 billion or 0.8 percent to $210.0 billion, following a
2.5 percent March increase. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.8 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $1.8 billion or 3.8 percent to $47.0 billion; decreases in motor vehicles
and parts and railroad equipment more than offset an increase in aircraft and parts. Primary metals decreased $0.2 billion or
1.6 percent to $15.8 billion. This is the largest decrease since April 1999. Electronic and other electrical equipment
decreased 0.1 percent to $38.7 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, led by computer and office equipment,
increased $1.4 billion or 3.4 percent to $42.7 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in April decreased $4.4 billion or 0.8 percent to $524.4 billion,
following a 1.6 percent March increase. This is the first decrease since June 1999. Electronic and other electrical
equipment had the largest decrease, $3.0 billion or 3.2 percent to $90.8 billion, due to electronic components. This is the
largest decrease since Julgf 1997. Transportation equipment, down twenty of the last twenty-four months, decreased $1.5
billion or 0.7 percent to $228.3 billion. Primary metals, down six consecutive months, decreased $0.2 billion or 0.8 percent
to $31.3 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, up ten consecutive months, increased $0.5 billion or 0.6 percent to
$85.6 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in April decreased $1.3 billion or 20.0 percent to $5.1
billion. This is the fourth consecutive decrease. Shipments, down four of the last five months, decreased $0.3 billion or 5.1
percent to $6.3 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $1.2 billion or 1.3 percent to $93.6 billion. This is the largest decrease
since August 1999.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in April increased $0.3 billion or 0.5 percent to $60.9
billion. This is the fourth increase in the last five months. Shipments, up four of the last five months, increased $1.6 billion
or 2.7 percent to $60.2 billion. Unfilled orders, up five consecutive months, increased $0.7 billion or 0.3 percent to $264.7
billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders increased $0.6 billion or 1.1 percent to $53.8 billion; shipments increased
$0.4 billion or 0.7 percent to $52.5 billion; and unfilled orders, up eight consecutive months, increased $1.3 billionor 1.1
percent to $122.1 billion.
e REVISED MARCH DATA Revised seasonally adjusted March figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments,
$377.4 billion (revised from $377.1 billion); new orders, $385.3 billion (revised from $383.2 billion); unfilled orders,
$554.5 billion (revised from $552.7 billion); and total inventories, $476.3 billion (revised from $476.2 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
August 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in August increased $6.1 billion or 2.9 percent to $216.1
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 13.1 percent July decrease and
is the third increase in the last four months. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 1.9 percent. Year-to-date, new
orders are 9.0 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $3.0 billion or 6.5 percent to $49.3 billion, due to aircraft and parts.
This is the third increase in the last four months. Electronic and other electrical equipment increased $1.1 billion or 2.8
percent to $39.2 billion, due to electronic components. Industrial machinery and equipment, up five of the last six months,
increased $0.7 billion or 1.5 percent to $46.5 billion. Primary metals decreased slightly, 0.2 percent to $15.6 billion.
o SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in August increased $2.3 billion or 1.1 percent to $214.7 billion, following a
2.4 percent July decrease. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.5 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $0.8 billion or 1.7 percent to $47.5 billion, due to aircraft and parts.
This is the third increase in the last four months. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up five of the last six months,
increased $0.4 billion or 1.0 percent to $41.2 billion, mostly due to communication equipment. Industrial machinery and
equipment increased $0.3 billion or 0.6 percent to $44.6 billion. Primary metals decreased $0.1 billion or 0.5 percent to
$15.8 billion.
o UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in August increased $1.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $555.3
billion, following a 0.4 percent July decrease. Industrial machinery and equipment, up fourteen consecutive months, had the
laréest increase, $1.9 billion or 2.1 percent to $91.9 billion. Transportation equipment increased $1.7 billion or 0.7 percent
to $244.2 billion. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $2.0 billion or 1.9 percent to $99.7 billion. Primary
metals decreased $0.3 billion or 0.8 percent to $30.7 billion. This is the tenth consecutive decrease.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in August increased $1.1 billion or 18.2 percent to $7.2
billion. This is the third increase in the last four months. Shipments decreased $0.3 billion or 3.9 percent to $6.3 billion.
This is the fourth decrease in the last five months. Unfilled orders increased $0.9 billion or 0.8 percent to $108.9 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in August increased $3.5 billion or 5.6 percent to
$65.8 billion. Shipments increased $2.9 billion or 4.8 percent to $63.8 billion. This is the largest increase since February
1996. Unfilled orders increased $2.0 billion or 0.7 percent to $275.5 billion. This is the eighth increase in the last nine
months. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders increased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to $55.6 billion; shipments, up six
consecutive months, increased $0.9 billion or 1.6 percent to $55.0 billion; and unfilled orders, up twelve consecutive
months, increased $0.6 billion or 0.5 percent to $129.0 billion.
e REVISED JULY DATA Revised seasonally adjusted July figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments, $377.9
billion (revised from $379.5 billion); new orders, $375.4 billion (revised from $377.6 billion); unfilled orders, $579.6 billion
(revised from $580.2 billion); and total inventories, $486.3 billion (revised from $485.2 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
December 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in December increased $4.6 billion or 2.2 percent to
$214.3 billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 1.8 percent November
increase. Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 1.4 percent. New orders for 2000 are 6.7 percent above 1999.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $6.9 billion or 14.6 percent to $54.2 billion, due to aircraft and parts.
Electronic and other electrical equipment increased $1.0 billion or 2.4 percent to $41.7 billion, due to electronic components.
Industrial machinery and equipment, down five consecutive months, decreased $2.3 billion or 5.3 percent to $40.9 billion.
Primary metals, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 3.5 percent to $14.3 billion; this is the largest
decrease since October 1998.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in December decreased $1.1 billion or 0.5 percent to $206.5 billion, following
a 1.1 percent November decrease. This is the third consecutive decrease. Shipments for 2000 are 5.2 percent above 1999.
Industrial machinery and equipment had the largest decrease, $1.1 billion or 2.5 percent to $41.8 billion, mostly due to
computer and office equipment. Transportation equipment, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.6 billion or 1.3
percent to $44.8 billion. Primary metals, down six consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 3.5 percent to $14.6
billion; this is the largest decrease since June 1996. Electronic and other electrical equipment increased $1.4 billion or 3.5
percent to $42.0 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in December increased $7.8 billion or 1.4 percent to $568.5
billion, following a 0.4 percent November increase. Transportation equipment had the largest increase, 89.4 billion or 3.8
percent to $258.6 billion, due to aircraft and parts. Industrial machinery and equipment, led by computer and office
equipment, decreased $0.9 billion or 1.0 percent to $91.5 billion; this is the largest decline since June 1999. Electronic and
other electrical equipment decreased $0.3 billion or 0.3 percent to $99.3 billion. Primary metals, down thirteen of the last
fourteen months, decreased $0.3 billion or 1.0 percent to $29.7 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in December decreased $2.2 billion or 25.9 percent to $6.2
billion. Shipments increased $0.2 billion or 2.7 percent to $6.7 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $0.5 billion or 0.4
percent to $110.6 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in December increased $7.2 billion or 11.6 percent to
$69.2 billion. Shipments decreased $0.7 billion or 1.2 percent to $61.0 billion. Unfilled orders, up six of the last seven
months, increased $8.2 billion or 2.9 percent to $287.9 billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders, down five of the
last six months, decreased $1.6 billion or 3.0 percent to $51.2 billion; shipments, down three consecutive months, decreased
$0.1 biilion or 0.3 percent to $53.1 billion; and unfilled orders, down three consecutive months following thirteen
consecutive increases, decreased $1.9 billion or 1.5 percent to $128.3 billion.
o REVISED NOVEMBER DATA Revised seasonally adjusted November figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $373.9 billion (revised from $374.1 billion); new orders, $376.2 billion (revised from $377.6 billion); unfilled
orders, $585.9 billion (revised from $587.1 billion); and total inventories, $494.2 billion (revised from $494.5 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
February 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in February decreased $4.9 billion or 2.3 percent to $208.4
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 2.2 percent January decrease.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 0.2 percent. Year-to-date, new orders are 6.6 percent above the same period
a year ago.
Transportation equipment, led by aircraft and parts, had the largest decrease, $4.5 billion or 8.7 percent to $47.1 billion.
This is the largest decrease since April 1999. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased $2.0 billion or 4.6 percent to
$40.6 billion. Primary metals decreased $0.4 billion or 2.4 percent to $15.7 billion. This is the largest decrease since
January 1999. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up seven of the last nine months, increased $2.4 billion or 6.4
percent to $39.7 billion.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in February decreased $3.9 billion or 1.8 percent to $205.7 billion, following
a 1.5 percent January increase. This is the first decrease since September 1999. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.9 percent
above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment, led by motor vehicles and parts, had the largest decrease, $1.9 billion or 4.0 percent to $46.7
billion. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased $1.5 billion or 3.5 percent to $39.9 billion. This is the largest
decrease since December 1991. Primary metals, down for the first time since October 1999, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.3
ercent to $15.9 billion. Electronic and other electrical equipment, down for the first time since October 1999, decreased
§O.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $37.8 billion.
o UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in February increased $2.7 billion or 0.5 percent to $519.0
billion, following a 0.7 percent January increase. This is the eighth consecutive increase. Electronic and other electrical
equipment had the largest increase, $1.9 billion or 2.2 percent to $86.7 billion, mostly due to electronic components. This is
the fourteenth increase in the last fifteenth months. Industrial machinery and equipment, up eight consecutive months,
increased $0.8 billion or 0.9 percent to $83.3 billion. Transportation equipment, up three consecutive months, increased
$0.4 billion or 0.2 percent to $230.9 billion, due to shipbuilding and tanks. Primary metals, down four consecutive months,
decreased $0.2 billion or 0.7 percent to $31.6 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in February decreased 0.6 percent to $6.8 billion.
Shipments, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.3 billion or 4.5 percent to $6.0 billion. Unfilled orders, up three
consecutive months, increased $0.8 billion or 0.8 percent to $95.1 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in February decreased $6.0 billion or 9.4 percent to
$57.4 billion. This is the largest decrease since December 1997. Shipments decreased $1.8 billion or 3.1 percent to $57.1
billion. Unfilled orders, up three consecutive months, increased $0.4 billion or 0.1 percent to $261.9 billion. Excluding
aircraft and parts, new orders decreased $4.0 billion or 7.5 percent to $50.0 billion, the largest decrease since October 1998;
shipments decreased $1.5 billion or 2.9 percent to $49.7 billion, the largest decrease since January 1996; and unfilled
orders, up six consecutive months, increased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $118.9 billion.
¢ REVISED JANUARY DATA Revised seasonally adjusted Januarg figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $370.4 billion (revised from $371.7 billion); new orders, $373.9 billion (revised from $375.2 billion); unfilled
orders, $541.7 billion (revised from $541.8 billion); and total inventories, $472.4 billion (revised from 471.9 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
JANUARY 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in January decreased $2.8 billion or 1.3 percent to $214.8
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 6.3 percent December increase.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 0.5 percent. New orders for January 2000 are 6.5 percent above January
1999.
Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest decrease, $5.5 billion or 13.2 percent to $36.0 billion. This is the
largest decrease since July 1997. Transportation equipment decreased $2.0 billion or 3.6 percent to $53.3 billion; decreases
in shipbuilding and tanks and aircraft and parts more than offset increases in motor vehicles and parts and railroad
equipment. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $4.7 billion or 12.3 percent to $43.1 billion. This is the largest
increase since February 1985. Primary metals increased $0.3 billion or 1.7 percent to $15.7 billion.
o SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in January increased $5.8 billion or 2.8 percent to $211.9 billion, following a
0.8 percent December increase. This is the eighth increase in the last nine months. Shipments for January 2000 are 9.2
percent above January 1999.
Industrial machinery and equipment, led by computer and office equipment, had the largest increase, $3.7 billion or 9.6
percent to $42.1 billion. This is the largest increase on record. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up three
consecutive months, increased $1.6 billion or 4.5 percent to $38.0 billion. Primary metals, up eight of the last nine months,
increased $0.2 billion or 1.4 percent to $16.0 billion. Transportation equipment decreased $0.6 billion or 1.2 percent to
$49.5 billion.
o UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in January increased $2.9 billion or 0.6 percent to $515.2
billion, following a 2.3 percent December increase. This is the seventh consecutive monthly increase. Transportation
equipment, led by aircraft and parts, had the largest increase, $3.8 billion or 1.7 percent to $230.9 billion. Industrial
machinery and equipment, up six of the last seven months, increased $1.0 billion or 1.3 percent to $82.3 billion. Electronic
and other electrical equipment, down for the first time since November 1998, decreased g 1.9 billion or 2.3 percent to $83.5
billion. Primary metals, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.3 billion or 0.8 percent to $31.8 billion.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in January decreased $2.9 billion or 28.7 percent to $7.1
billion. Shipments decreased $0.2 billion or 3.2 percent to $6.3 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.8 billion or 0.8 percent
to $95.7 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in January increased $3.6 billion or 6.0 percent to
$64.5 billion. Shipments increased $3.5 billion or 6.3 percent to $59.8 billion. This is the largest increase since February
1996. Unfilled orders increased $4.7 billion or 1.8 percent to $260.2 billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders
increased $3.8 billion or 7.5 percent to $54.8 billion; shipments increased $4.0 billion or 8.3 percent to $52.0 billion, the
largest increase on record; and unfilled orders, up five consecutive months, increased $2.8 billion or 2.4 percent to $118.4
billion.
¢ REVISED DECEMBER DATA Revised seasonally adjusted December figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $367.7 billion (revised from $367.4 billion); new orders, $379.2 billion (revised from $377.8 billion); unfilled
orders, $538.2 billion (revised from $537.0 billion); and total inventories, $470.6 billion (revised from $471.0 billion).

¢ NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in July decreased $30.0 billion or 12.4 percent to $212.4
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 9.5 percent June increase and is
the largest decrease on record. Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 4.8 percent. Year-to-date, new orders are
9.9 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $21.7 billion or 31.7 percent to $46.8 billion, mostly due to aircraft and
parts. This is the largest decrease on record. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $7.9 billion or 16.8
percent to $39.1 billion, due to electronic components and communication equipment. Primary metals decreased $0.2 billion
or 1.4 percent to $15.8 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, up four of the last five months, increased $1.9 billion
or 4.3 percent to $46.0 billion.
¢ SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in July decreased $4.1 billion or 1.9 percent to $214.1 billion, following a 1.6
percent June increase. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.9 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $4.9 billion or 9.3 percent to $47.4 billion; all component industries
decreased. This 1s the largest decrease since the 9.9 percent decline in July 1993. Electronic and other electrical equipment,
down following four consecutive increases, decreased $0.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $41.1 billion. Primary metals decreased
$0.1 billion or 0.4 percent to $16.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $1.7 billion or 4.1 percent to
$44.2 billion. This is the fourth increase in the last five months.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in July decreased $1.7 billion or 0.3 percent to $554.7 billion,
following a 4.6 percent June increase. Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest decrease, $2.0 billion or 1.9
percent to $102.3 billion, due to electronic components. Transportation equipment, down five of the last six months,
decreased $0.6 billion or 0.3 percent to $242.3 billion. Primary metals, down nine consecutive months, decreased $0.3
billion or 0.8 percent to $31.1 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $1.7 billion or 1.9 percent to $90.2
billion. This is the thirteenth consecutive increase.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in July decreased $14.9 billion or 72.0 percent to $5.8
billion. This is the largest decrease on record. Shipments decreased $0.5 billion or 7.2 percent to $6.5 billion. This is the
sixth decrease in the last eight months. Unfilled orders decreased $0.7 billion or 0.7 percent to $107.7 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in July decreased $8.8 billion or 12.3 percent to $62.6
billion. This is the largest decrease since December 1997. Shipments decreased $1.5 billion or 2.4 percent to $60.9 billion.
Unfilled orders increased $1.7 billion or 0.6 percent to $273.8 billion. This is the seventh increase in the last eight months.
Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders decreased $2.2 billion or 3.8 percent to $55.8 billion; shipments, up five
consecutive months, increased $0.1 billion or 0.2 percent to $54.1 billion; and unfilled orders, up eleven consecutive months,
increased $1.8 billion or 1.4 percent to $128.8 billion.

June 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in June increased $22.1 billion or 10.0 percent to $243.2
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today_. This follows a 7.0 percent May increase and is
the largest increase since July 1991. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 0.8 percent. Year-to-date, new orders
are 11.1 percent above the same period a year ago; new orders for the second quarter are 4.3 percent above the first quarter.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $20.8 billion or 43.0 percent to $69.1 billion, mostly due to aircraft and
arts. This is the largest increase on record. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $0.6 billion or 1.3 percent to
I$?44.l billion. Primary metals increased $0.3 billion or 1.6 percent to $16.1 billion. Electronic and other electrical
equipment, up four of the last five months, increased $0.1 billion or 0.3 percent to $47.1 billion.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in June increased $3.3 billion or 1.5 percent to $218.1 billion, following a 2.6
percent May increase. Year-to-date, shipments are 7.2 percent above the same period a year ago; shipments for the second
quarter are 2.4 percent above the first quarter. ‘
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $2.8 billion or 5.6 percent to $52.7 billion, due to motor vehicles and
parts, and railroad equipment. Electronic and other electrical equipment increased $0.7 billion or 1.7 percent to $41.1
billion. This is the seventh increase in the last eight months. Primary metals increased $0.1 billion or 0.5 percent to $16.1
billion. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased $0.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $42.2 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in June increased $25.1 billion or 4.7 percent to $557.0 billion,
following a 1.2 percent May increase. This is the eleventh increase in the last twelve months and the largest on record.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $16.5 billion or 7.3 percent to $243.1 billion, due to aircraft and parts.
This is the largest increase on record. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up seventeen of the last nineteen months,
increased $6.0 billion or 6.1 percent to $104.2 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, up twelve consecutive months,
increased $1.9 billion or 2.2 percent to $88.9 billion. Primary metals increased $0.1 billion or 0.2 percent to $31.5 billion.
This is the first increase since October 1999.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in June increased $13.8 billion or 194.1 percent to $20.9
billion. This is the largest increase on record. Shipments increased $0.8 billion or 12.8 percent to $7.0 billion. This is the
largest increase since June 1971. Unfilled orders increased $13.9 billion or 14.7 percent to $108.6 billion. This is the
largest increase on record.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in June increased $10.2 billion or 16.8 percent to
$71.1 billion. This is the largest increase since December 1992. Shipments, down for the first time since February,
decreased $0.2 billion or 0.3 percent to $62.4 billion. Unfilled orders, increased $8.7 billion or 3.3 percent to $271.8
billion. This is the largest increase since November 1997. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders increased $4.3 billion or
8.0 percent to $57.9 billion (the largest increase since July 1999); shipments, up four consecutive months, increased $0.8
billion or 1.5 percent to $53.9 billion; and unfilled orders, up ten consecutive months, increased $4.0 billion or 3.3 percent
to $127.0 billion.

May 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
o NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in May increased $12.3 billion or 6.0 percent to $218.9
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 5.7 percent April decrease and
is the largest increase since December 1999. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 6.6 percent. Year-to-date, new
orders are 8.4 percent above the same period a year ago.
Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest increase, $9.6 billion or 26.0 percent to $46.5 billion, due to
electronic components. This is the largest increase since August 1997. Transportation equipment increased $1.6 billion or
3.5 percent to $46.9 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts and shipbuilding and tanks. Primary metals increased $0.2
billion or 1.1 percent to $15.9 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased 0.1 percent to $43.6 billion.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in May increased $4.5 billion or 2.2 percent to $213.9 billion, following a 1.0
percent April decrease. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.8 percent above the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $2.9 billion or 6.2 percent to $49.5 billion; all components increased, led
by aircraft and parts and motor vehicles and parts. This is the largest increase since August 1998. Electronic and other
electrical equipment increased $1.0 billion or 2.6 percent to $40.0 billion. This is the sixth increase in the last seven
months. Primary metals increased $0.1 billion or 0.9 percent to $16.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment
decreased $0.6 billion or 1.3 percent to $42.2 billion.
o UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in May increased $5.0 billion or 1.0 percent to $530.7 billion,
following a 0.5 percent April decrease. This is the tenth increase in the last eleven months. Electronic and other electrical
equipment had the largest increase, $6.4 billion or 7.0 percent to $98.1 billion, due to electronic components. This is the
largest increase since August 1997. Industrial machinery and equipment, up eleven consecutive months, increased $1.4
billion or 1.6 percent to §87.2 billion. Transportation equipment, down fourteen of the last sixteen months, decreased $2.6
billion or 1.1 percent to $225.6 billion. Primary metals, down seven consecutive months, decreased $0.1 billion or 0.2
percent to $31.4 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in May increased $0.6 billion or 11.7 dpercent to $6.1
billion. This is the first increase since December 1999. Shipments, down five of the last six months, decreased $0.1 billion
or 1.2 percent to $6.2 billion. Unfilled orders, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to
$93.8 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in May decreased $1.0 billion or 1.6 percent to $60.5
billion. Shipments, up three consecutive months, increased $1.8 billion or 3.0 percent to $62.3 billion. Unfilled orders,
down for the first time since November 1999, decreased $1.7 billion or 0.7 percent to $263.0 billion. Excluding aircraft and
arts, new orders decreased $1.1 billion or 2.1 percent to $53.3 billion; shipments, up three consecutive months, increased
50.2 billion or 0.3 percent to $52.9 billion; and unfilled orders, up nine consecutive months, increased $0.4 billion or 0.4
percent to $122.9 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
October 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)

® NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in October decreased $12.1 billion or 5.5 percent to $209.0
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 2.4 percent September increase.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 2.2 percent. Year-to-date, new orders are 8.3 percent above the same period
a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $8.4 billion or 15.8 percent to $44.9 billion, mostly due to aircraft and
parts. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $4.3 billion or 9.9 percent to $39.1 billion, mostly due to
electronic components. Primary metals decreased $0.5 billion or 3.2 percent to $15.3 billion; this is the largest decrease’
since December 1998. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $0.8 billion or 1.8 percent to $44.2 billion.

¢ SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in October decreased $1.8 billion or 0.8 percent to $212.4 billion, following a
0.1 percent September increase. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.2 percent above the same period a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $2.3 billion or 4.7 percent to $46.3 billion, mostly due to aircraft and
parts and motor vehicles and parts. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $0.3 billion or 0.8 percent to $41.4
billion. Primary metals, down four consecutive months, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.3 percent to $15.5 billion. Industrial
machinery and equipment increased $0.8 billien or 1.9 percent to $44.0 billion.

® UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in October decreased $3.4 billion or 0.6 percent to $559.3
billion, following a 1.2 percent September increase. This is the largest decrease since June 1999. Electronic and other
electrical equipment had the largest decrease, $2.2 billion or 2.2 percent to $99.9 billion, mostly due to electronic
components. Transportation equipment, led by aircraft and parts, decreased $1.4 billion or 0.6 percent to $247.6 billion.
Primary metals, down eleven of the last twelve months, decreased $0.3 billion or 0.9 percent to $30.3 billion. Industrial
machinery and equipment increased $0.1 billion or 0.2 percent to $92.4 billion. This is the sixteenth consecutive increase.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in October increased $0.8 billion or 13.1 percent to $6.8
billion. Shipments decreased $0.1 billion or 1.8 percent to $6.2 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.6 billion or 0.5
percent to $109.3 billion.

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in October decreased $7.8 billion or 11.3 percent to
$60.7 billion. Shipments decreased $0.4 billion or 0.6 percent to $62.4 billion. Unfilled orders, down for the first time
since May, decreased: $1.6 billion or 0.6 percent to $279.8 billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders decreased $0.3
billion or 0.5 percent to $55.3 billion; shipments, up seven of the last eight months, increased $0.7 billion or 1.4 percent to
$55.0 billion; and unfilled orders, up fourteen consecutive months, increased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $131.1 billion.
¢ REVISED SEPTEMBER DATA Revised seasonally adjusted September figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $380.2 billion (revised from $380.4 billion); new orders, $387.2 billion (revised from $388.6 billion); unfilled
orders, $588.2 billion (revised from $589.4 billion); and total inventories, $488.5 billion (unrevised).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
September 2000
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
o NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in September increased $3.8 billion or 1.8 percent to
$221.0 billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 3.5 percent August
increase and is the fourth increase in the last five months. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 0.8 percent.
Year-to-date, new orders are 8.9 percent above the same period a year ago; new orders for the third quarter are 3.2 percent
below the second quarter.
Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest increase, $4.8 billion or 11.8 percent to $45.3 billion, due to
electronic components and communication equipment. Transportation equipment, up four of the last five months, increased
$2.5 billion or 5.1 percent to $51.9 billion; led by aircraft and parts, all components increased. Primary metals increased
$0.5 billion or 3.4 percent to $16.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, down for the first time since May,
decreased $3.3 billion or 7.1 percent to $42.9 billion. This is the largest decrease since October 1998.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in September increased $0.3 billion or 0.2 percent to $214.4 billion, following
a 0.9 percent August increase. This is the fourth increase in the last five months. Year-to-date, shipments are 6.4 percent
above the same period a year ago; shipments for the third quarter are 0.2 percent below the second quarter.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $0.9 billion or 1.9 percent to $48.6 billion, led by motor vehicles and
parts. This is the fourth increase in the last five months. Electronic and other electrical equipment, up six of the last seven
months, increased $0.8 billion or 1.8 percent to $42.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, down four of the last
five months, decreased $0.7 billion or 1.6 percent to $42.9 billion. Primary metals, down three consecutive months,
decreased 0.3 percent to $15.8 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in September increased $6.6 billion or 1.2 percent to $563.7
billion, following a 0.6 percent August increase. This is the thirteenth increase in the last fifteen months. Transportation
equipment had the largest increase, $3.4 billion or 1.4 percent to $247.5 billion, due to aircraft and parts. Electronic and
other electrical equipment increased $3.2 billion or 3.2 percent to $104.1 billion. Primary metals increased $0.2 billion or
0.7 percent to $30.8 billion. This is the first increase since October 1999. Industrial machinery and equipment increased
slightly to $92.8 billion. This is the fifteenth consecutive increase.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in September decreased $0.4 billion or 5.6 percent to $6.9
billion. Shipments increased $0.1 billion or 1.7 percent to $6.4 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.5 billion or 0.5 percent
to $109.5 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in September increased $1.7 billion or 2.6 percent to
$67.3 billion. Shipments decreased $0.2 billion or 0.3 percent to $62.6 billion. Unfilled orders increased $4.7 billion or 1.7
percent to $281.0 billion. This is the ninth increase in the last ten months. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders, down
three consecutive months, decreased $0.4 billion or 0.8 percent to $55.0 billion; shipments, up six of the last seven months,
increased $0.1 billion or 0.2 percent to $54.0 billion; and unfilled orders, up thirteen consecutive months, increased $0.9
billion or 0.7 percent to $130.9 billion.
¢ REVISED AUGUST DATA Revised seasonally adjusted August figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments,
$381.0 billion (revised from $381.4 billion); new orders, $383.9 billion (revised from $382.5 billion); unfilled orders,
$582.5 billion (revised from $580.7 billion); and total inventories, $487.8 billion (revised from $487.6 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
April 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
o NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in April decreased $9.8 billion or 5.0 percent to $184.7 billion, the
Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 2.2 percent March increase. Excluding
transportation, new orders decreased 3.3 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2001 are 8.2 percent below the same period a
year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $5.4 billion or 9.3 percent to $52.4 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts
decreased $1.6 billion or 14.6 percent to $9.1 billion. Computers and electronic products, led by semiconductors, decreased
$3.6 billion or 8.8 percent to $37.6 billion; this is the fourth decrease in the last five months. Machinery, down three
consecutive months, decreased $0.7 billion or 2.8 percent to $23.7 billion.
e SHIPMENTS of durable goods in April decreased $6.9 billion or 3.6 percent to $185.9 billion, following a 0.3 percent
March decrease. This is the fourth consecutive decrease and the largest since February 2000. Year to date, shipments for 2001
are 5.2 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $3.3 billion or 6.2 percent to $49.1 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts
decreased $1.2 billion or 13.8 percent to $7.2 billion. Computers and electronic products, down four consecutive months,
decreased $2.1 billion or 5.1 percent to $40.2 billion. Machinery, down three consecutive months, decreased $0.8 billion or 3.1
percent to $24.2 billion. Primary metals, down ten consecutive months, decreased $0.4 billion or 3.5 percent to $11.6 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS for durable goods in April decreased $1.2 billion or 0.2 percent to $587.1 billion, following a 0.3
percent March increase. Computers and electronic products, led by semiconductors, had the largest decrease, $2.7 billion or
1.8 percent to $144.5 billion; this is the fifth consecutive decrease. Machinery, down four consecutive months, decreased $0.4
billion or 0.7 percent to $62.9 billion. Transportation increased $3.3 billion or 1.1 percent to $288.8 billion; nondefense aircraft
and parts increased $1.9 billion or 1.3 percent to $152.1 billion.
e INVENTORIES for durable goods in April increased $0.3 billion or 0.1 percent to $308.0 billion, following a 0.9 percent
March decrease. Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $1.0 billion or 1.4 percent to $76.2 billion; nondefense
aircraft and parts increased $0.1 billion or 0.5 percent to $31.1 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in April decreased $1.7 billion or 20.4 percent to $6.5 billion.
Shipments decreased $0.1 billion or 2.4 percent to $5.7 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.8 billion or 0.7 percent to $125.4
billion. Inventories increased $0.6 billion or 3.5 percent to $19.1 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in April decreased $3.6 billion or 5.2 percent to $65.2
billion. Shipments decreased $3.2 billion or 4.7 percent to $65.3 billion. Unfilled orders decreased slightly to $279.6 billion.
Inventories decreased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $131.6 billion.
e REVISED MARCH DATA Revised seasonally adjusted March figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments,
$346.6 billion (revised from $347.8 billion); new orders, $348.3 billion (revised from $349.6 billion); unfilled orders, $588.3
billion (revised from $588.4 billion); and total inventories, $481.5 billion (revised from $481.7 billion).

DECEMBER 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)

® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in December increased $3.4 billion or 2.0 percent to $176.4 billion, the
Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 6.0 percent November decrease. Excluding
transportation, new orders increased 1.4 percent. New orders for 2001 were 12.8 percent below 2000; new orders for the fourth
quarter were 1.4 percent above the third quarter.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $1.7 billion or 3.5 percent to $49.8 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts
increased $1.2 billion or 26.9 percent to $5.7 billion. Computers and electronic products, led by semiconductors, increased $1.1
billion or 3.5 percent to $33.4 billion.
® SHIPMENTS of durable goods in December increased $0.9 billion or 0.5 percent to $180.5 billion. This follows a 0.4 percent
November decrease. Shipments for 2001 were 8.1 percent below 2000; shipments for the fourth quarter were 1.3 percent below the
third quarter.
Transportation equipment, up three consecutive months, had the largest increase, $0.9 billion or 1.6 percent to $53.9 billion;
nondefense aircraft and parts decreased $0.1 billion or 1.3 percent to $8.4 billion. Computers and electronic products, up three
consecutive months, increased $0.5 billion or 1.6 percent to $33.8 billion. Machinery decreased $0.4 billion or 1.8 percent to
$22.4 billion. Primary metals, down four of the last five months, decreased $0.3 billion or 3.1 percent to $10.9 billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS for durable goods in December, down eleven of the last twelve months, decreased $4.0 billion or 0.7
percent to $545.9 billion. This follows a 1.2 percent November decrease.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $4.1 billion or 1.5 percent to $277.8 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts
decreased $2.7 billion or 2.0 percent to $134.1 billion. Computers and electronic products, down thirteen consecutive months,
decreased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $125.5 billion. Machinery increased $0.5 billion or 0.9 percent to $58.2 billion.
® INVENTORIES for durable goods in December, down eleven consecutive months, decreased $1.2 billion or 0.4 percent to
$284.7 billion. Computers and electronic products, down ten consecutive months, had the largest decrease, $1.3 billion or 2.5
percent to $49.8 billion. Transportation equipment increased $1.1 billion or 1.5 percent to $74.4 billion; nondefense aircraft and
parts decreased $0.2 billion or 0.7 percent to $31.0 billion.

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in December increased $0.6 billion or 10.8 percent to $6.4 billion.
Shipments increased $1.0 billion or 16.0 percent to $7.4 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $1.0 billion or 0.7 percent to $133.6
billion. Inventories increased $0.2 billion or 1.2 percent to $18.8 billion.

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in December increased $0.7 billion or 1.3 percent to $57.2
billion. Shipments increased $0.4 billion or 0.6 percent to $59.6 billion. Unfilled orders, down twelve consecutive months,
decreased $2.5 billion or 1.0 percent to $246.8 billion. Inventories, down eleven consecutive months, decreased $1.2 billion or 1.0
percent to $121.0 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
February 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in February decreased $0.4 billion or 0.2 percent to $199.2
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 7.3 percent January decrease.
Excluding transportation, new orders increased 0.5 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2001 are 6.0 percent below the
same period a year ago.
Transportation equiFment had the largest decrease, $1.1 billion or 2.6 percent to $41.4 billion; all component industries
declined. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased $1.1 billion or 2.4 percent to $42.6 billion. Primary metals, down
five consecutive months, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.1 percent to $13.9 billion. Electronic and other electrical equipment
increased $2.2 billion or 6.0 percent to $39.4 billion, due to electronic components.
e SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in February decreased $0.6 billion or 0.3 percent to $200.9 billion, following
a 2.5 percent January decrease. This is the fifth consecutive decrease. Year to date, shipments for 2001 are 3.3 percent
below the same period a year ago.
Industrial machinery and equipment, led by computer and office equipment, had the largest decrease, $1.6 billion or 3.6
percent to $41.8 billion. This is the largest decrease since December 1991. Primary metals, down eight consecutive
months, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.4 percent to $14.3 billion. Transportation equipment, up for the first time since
September 2000, increased $1.4 billion or 3.5 percent to $42.6 billion, due to aircraft and parts. Electronic and other
electrical equipment increased 0.1 percent to $40.4 billion.
o UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in February decreased $1.7 billion or 0.3 percent to $568.4
billion, following a 0.3 percent January decrease. Transportation equipment, led by aircraft and parts, had the largest
decrease, $1.2 billion or 0.4 percent to $262.6 billion. Electronic and other electrical equipment, down three consecutive
months, decreased $1.0 billion or 1.1 percent to $94.7 billion, due to electronic components. Primary metals, down fifteen
of the last sixteen months, decreased $0.4 billion or 1.2 percent to $28.8 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment
increased $0.9 billion or 1.0 percent to $93.0 billion, due to engines and turbines.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in February increased $1.6 billion or 28.8 percent to $7.0
billion. Shipments decreased $0.1 billion or 1.4 percent to $6.4 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.6 billion or 0.6
percent to $110.2 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in February decreased $4.1 billion or 6.4 percent to
$59.6 billion. Shipments increased $0.3 billion or 0.4 percent to $60.3 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $0.7 billion or
0.2 percent to $295.0 billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders, down four of the last five months, decreased $2.2
billion or 4.0 percent to $52.1 billion; shipments, down four of the last five months, decreased $1.4 billion or 2.6 percent to
$51.4 billion; and unfilled orders increased $0.7 billion or 0.5 percent to $131.0 billion.
o REVISED JANUARY DATA Revised seasonally adjusted Janua:g figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $366.9 billion (revised from $368.0 billion); new orders, $364.9 billion (revised from $366.5 billion); unfilled
orders, $595.1 billion (revised from $595.6 billion); and total inventories, $496.0 billion (revised from $496.3 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
January 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in January decreased $12.9 billion or 6.0 percent to $202.0
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 1.2 percent December increase.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 0.3 percent. New orders for January 2001 are 5.6 percent below
January 2000.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $12.5 billion or 22.4 percent to $43.2 billion; led by aircraft and garts,
all component industries declined. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $2.5 billion or 6.2 percent to $38.0
billion, due to electronic components. Primary metals, down four consecutive months, decreased $0.1 billion or 0.6 percent
to $14.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment, led by computer and office equipment, increased $2.4 billion or 5.7
percent to $44.1 billion; this is the largest increase since January 2000.
® SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in January decreased $3.5 billion or 1.7 percent to $203.0 billion, following a
0.6 percent December decrease. This is the fourth consecutive decrease. Shipments for January 2001 are 3.1 percent below
January 2000.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $3.3 billion or 7.3 percent to $41.6 billion; led by motor vehicles and
arts, all component industries declined. Electronic and other electrical equipment decreased $1.0 billion or 2.3 percent to
540.6 billion; this is the largest decrease since April 1998. Primary metals, down seven consecutive months, decreased $0.1

billion or 0.5 percent to $14.5 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $1.1 billion or 2.7 percent to $43.6
billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in January decreased $1.0 billion or 0.2 percent to $570.8
billion, following a 1.5 percent December increase. Electronic and other electrical equipment had the largest decrease, $2.6
billion or 2.6 percent to $96.2 billion, due to electronic components. Primary metals, down fourteen of the last fifteen
months, decreased $0.4 billion or 1.4 percent to $29.2 billion. Transportation equipment increased $1.5 billion or 0.6
percent to $263.7 billion, due to aircraft and parts. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $0.5 billion or 0.5 percent
to $92.2 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in January decreased $0.5 billion or 7.3 percent to $5.8
billion. Shipments increased 0.1 percent to $6.7 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $0.9 billion or 0.8 percent to $109.7
billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in January decreased $6.4 billion or 8.9 percent to
$65.2 billion. Shipments, down six of the last eight months, decreased $0.7 billion or 1.1 percent to $61.1 billion. Unfilled
orders, up seven of the last eight months, increased $4.1 billion or 1.4 percent to $295.9 billion. Excluding aircraft and
parts, new orders, up for the first time since September 2000, increased $3.4 billion or 6.5 percent to $55.1 billion;
shipments, down four consecutive months, decreased slightly to $53.4 billion; and unfilled orders, up for the first time since
September 2000, increased $1.8 billion or 1.4 percent to $130.5 billion.
e REVISED DECEMBER DATA Revised seasonally adjusted December figures for all manufacturing industries are:
shipments, $372.1 billion (revised from $372.9 billion); new orders, $380.5 billion (revised from $382.5 billion); unfilled
orders, $596.8 billion (revised from $598.0 billion); and total inventories, $493.3 billion (revised from $493.6 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
July 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
o NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in July decreased $1.2 billion or 0.6 percent to $182.0 billion, the
Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 2.6 percent June decrease. Excluding
transportation, new orders decreased 1.4 percent. Year to date, new orders are 11.6 percent below the same period a year ago.
Computers and electronic products had the largest decrease, $1.5 billion or 4.4 percent to $32.5 billion, due to semiconductors.
Machinery decreased $0.7 billion or 3.0 percent to $23.5 billion. Transportation equipment increased $0.7 billion or 1.3
percent to $53.0 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts; nondefense aircraft and parts decreased $0.9 billion or 10.6 percent to
$7.6 billion.
o SHIPMENTS of durable goods in July increased $0.3 billion or 0.2 percent to $187.9 billion, following a 2.5 percent June
decrease. Year to date, shipments are 6.2 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $0.7 billion or 1.4 percent to $54.4 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts;
nondefense aircraft and parts decreased $0.4 billion or 4.6 percent to $8.5 billion. Machinery increased $0.4 billion or 1.5
percent to $24.6 billion. Computers and electronic products, led by nondefense communications equipment and semiconductors,
decreased $1.2 billion or 3.4 percent to $35.7 billion; this is the seventh consecutive decrease. Electrical equipment decreased
$0.4 billion or 3.8 percent to $10.5 billion; this is the largest decrease since September 1999.
¢ UNFILLED ORDERS for durable goods in July, down seven consecutive months, decreased $5.9 billion or 1.0 percent to
$568.2 billion, following a 0.8 percent June decrease; this is the largest decrease since January. Computers and electronic
products, led by semiconductors, had the largest decrease, $3.3 billion or 2.4 percent to $133.1 billion; this is the eighth
consecutive decrease. Transportation equipment decreased $1.4 billion or 0.5 percent to $286.2 billion; nondefense aircraft and
parts decreased $1.0 billion or 0.6 percent to $149.9 billion. Machinery, down six of the last seven months, decreased $1.0
billion or 1.6 percent to $60.3 billion.
e INVENTORIES for durable goods in July, down six consecutive months, decreased $1.9 billion or 0.6 percent to
$299.0 billion, following a 1.1 percent June decrease. Computers and electronic products, down five consecutive months, had
the largest decrease, $0.8 billion or 1.4 percent to $56.8 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in July increased $0.8 billion or 15.6 percent to $6.3 billion.
Shipments decreased $0.3 billion or 4.1 percent to $6.4 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to $123.8
billion. Inventories decreased 0.3 percent to $18.2 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in July, down four consecutive months, decreased $1.2
billion or 1.9 percent to $60.2 billion. Shipments, down four of the last five months, decreased $1.1 billion or 1.7 percent to
$63.6 billion. Unfilled orders, down seven consecutive months, decreased $3.4 billion or 1.2 percent to $268.3 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS AND ORDERS
March 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
e NEW ORDERS New orders for manufactured durable goods in March increased $6.1 billion or 3.0 percent to $205.1
billion, the Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 0.3 percent February decrease.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 1.8 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2001 are 6.2 percent below the
same period a year ago; new orders for the first quarter are 4.7 percent below the fourth quarter.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $8.9 billion or 21.4 percent to $50.7 billion; led by shipbuilding and
tanks, all component industries increased. Electronic and other electrical equipment, led by electronic components,
decreased $2.1 billion or 5.3 percent to $37.4 billion. Industrial machinery and equipment decreased $0.3 billion or 0.7
percent to $41.9 billion. Primary metals, down six consecutive months, decreased $0.2 billion or 1.7 percent to $13.7
billion.
o SHIPMENTS Shipments of durable goods in March increased $0.2 billion or 0.1 percent to $199.9 billion, following a
0.9 percent February decrease. This is the first increase since September 2000. Year to date, shipments for 2001 are 4.2
percent below the same period a year ago; shipments for the first quarter are 3.7 percent below the fourth quarter.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $1.4 billion or 3.4 percent to $44.2 billion; led by motor vehicles and
parts, all component industries increased. Industrial machinery and equipment increased $0.3 billion or 0.6 percent to $41.5
billion. Electronic and other electrical equipment, down five of the last six months, decreased $1.1 billion or 2.8 percent to
$38.7 billion, mostly due to electronic components. Primary metals, down nine consecutive months, decreased $0.1 billion
or 1.0 percent to $14.1 billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS Unfilled orders for durable goods in March increased $5.2 billion or 0.9 percent to $574.5
billion, following a 0.1 percent Februa,.rg decrease. Transportation equipment, led by shipbuilding and tanks, had the largest
increase, $6.5 billion or 2.5 percent to $269.0 billion. Industrial machinery and equi{pment, up three consecutive months,
increased $0.5 billion or 0.5 percent to $93.4 billion, due to engines and turbines. Electronic and other electrical equipment,
down four consecutive months, decreased $1.3 billion or 1.4 percent to $94.0 billion. Primary metals, down sixteen of the
last seventeen months, decreased $0.4 billion or 1.4 percent to $28.5 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in March increased $4.3 billion or 62.0 percent to $11.2
billion. Shipments increased $0.1 billion or 1.2 percent to $6.4 billion. Unfilled orders increased $4.7 billion or 4.3 percent
to $114.9 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in March increased $3.1 billion or 5.2 percent to
$62.2 billion. Shipments increased $0.7 billion or 1.3 percent to $60.2 billion. Unfilled orders increased $2.1 billion or
0.7 percent to $297.3 billion. Excluding aircraft and parts, new orders, down five of the last six months, decreased $0.4
billion or 0.7 percent to $51.2 billion; shipments increased $0.8 billion or 1.6 percent to $51.4 billion; and unfilled orders
decreased $0.2 billion or 0.1 percent to $131.0 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
May 2001
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in May increased $5.3 billion or 2.9 percent to $188.5 billion, the
Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This follows a 5.5 percent April decrease. Excluding
transportation, new orders increased 2.7 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2001 are 8.9 percent below the same period a
year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $1.8 billion or 3.4 percent to $54.5 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts;
nondefense aircraft and parts decreased $1.0 billion or 11.8 percent to $7.8 billion. Computers and electronic products
increased $1.0 billion or 2.7 percent to $35.8 billion, due to semiconductors. Primary metals increased $0.7 billion or 5.9
gercent to $12.4 billion; this is the largest increase since February 1999. Machinery increased $0.6 billion or 2.6 percent to
24.7 billion.
¢ SHIPMENTS of durable goods in May increased $5.8 billion or 3.1 percent to $192.4 billion, following a 3.8 percent April
decrease. Year to date, shipments for 2001 are 5.3 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment, led by motor vehicles and parts, had the ]argest increase, $4.5 billion or 9.2 percent to $53.9 billion;
nondefense aircraft and parts increased $1.2 billion or 17.0 percent to $8.3 billion. Primary metals increased $0.5 billion or 4.6
percent to $12.3 billion; this is the largest increase since December 1994. Machinery, up for the first time since January,
increased $0.4 billion or 1.5 percent to $25.2 billion. Computers and electronic products, down five consecutive months,
decreased $0.7 billion or 1.7 percent to $38.5 billion.
e UNFILLED ORDERS for durable goods in May, down five consecutive months, decreased $3.9 billion or 0.7 percent to
$579.2 billion, following a 0.6 percent April decrease. Computers and electronic products, led by semiconductors, had the
largest decrease, $2.7 billion or 1.9 percent to $139.3 billion; this is the sixth consecutive decrease. Machinery, down five
consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 0.8 percent to $61.3 billion. Transportation equipment increased $0.6 billion or
0.2 percent to $289.6 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts decreased $0.5 billion or 0.4 percent to $151.5 billion.
® INVENTORIES for durable goods in May, down four consecutive months, decreased $1.6 billion or 0.5 percent to $304.9
billion, following a 0.2 percent April decrease. Computers and electronic products had the largest decrease, $0.5 billion or 0.9
percent to $58.4 billion. Nondefense aircraft and parts increased $0.1 billion or 0.3 percent to $31.3 billion.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in May increased 0.1 percent to $6.3 billion. Shipments
increased $0.2 billion or 3.9 percent to $6.0 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.3 billion or 0.2 percent to $125.3 billion.
Inventories decreased 0.1 percent to $19.0 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in May increased $0.6 billion or 0.9 percent to $65.2
billion. Shipments increased $1.3 billion or 2.0 percent to $66.8 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $1.6 billion or 0.6 percent
to $276.0 billion. Inventories decreased $0.2 billion or 0.1 percent to $130.8 billion.
® REVISED APRIL DATA Revised seasonally adjusted April figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments, $339.1
billion (revised from $338.9 billion); new orders, $335.7 billion (revised from $336.9 billion); unfilled orders, $583.1 billion
(revised from $584.5 billion); and total inventories, $479.9 billion (revised from $481.0 billion).

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
April 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
¢ NEW ORDERS, excluding semiconductors, for manufactured durable goods in April increased $1.9 billion or 1.1 percent to $176.6
billion, the Department of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 0.2 percent March increase. Excluding
transportation, new orders increased 2.9 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 3.9 percent below the same period a year ago.
Machinery had the largest increase, $0.9 billion or 4.0 percent to $22.7 billion, led by turbines and generators. Electrical equipment,
appliances, and components increased $0.7 billion or 7.6 percent to $10.0 billion. Primary metals increased $0.6 billion or 5.1 percent to
$11.6 billion. Transportation equipment decreased $1.5 billion or 2.6 percent to $54.8 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts decreased
22.3 percent to $5.8 billion.
® SHIPMENTS, excluding semiconductors, of durable goods in April increased $6.0 billion or 3.5 percent to $179.1 billion. This
followed a 0.5 percent March increase. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 4.1 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $4.3 billion or 8.1 percent to $57.1 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts decreased 3.2
percent to $7.8 billion. Fabricated metal products increased $0.5 billion or 2.3 percent to $20.2 billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS, excluding semiconductors, for durable goods in April decreased $2.5 billion or 0.5 percent to $522.5 billion.
This followed a 0.3 percent March increase.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $2.2 billion or 0.8 percent to $277.6 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts, down
twelve consecutive months, decreased $2.0 billion or 1.5 percent to $127.9 billion. Machinery, down four consecutive months, decreased
$0.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $54.0 billion.
® INVENTORIES, excluding semiconductors, for durable goods in April, down fifteen consecutive months, decreased $0.8 billion or
0.3 percent to $267.7 billion. This followed a 1.0 percent March decrease.
Machinery had the largest decrease, $0.3 billion or 0.6 percent to $47.3 billion, primarily due to metalworking machinery.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in April decreased $3.6 billion or 33.3 percent to $7.1 billion.
Shipments increased $0.1 billion or 1.2 percent to $7.1 billion. Unfilled orders increased slightly to $136.6 billion. Inventories increased
$0.1 billion or 0.3 percent to $18.7 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in April increased $1.1 billion or 1.9 percent to $56.6 billion.
Shipments decreased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to $59.0 billion. Unfilled orders, down sixteen consecutive months, decreased $2.4
billion or 1.0 percent to $232.8 billion. Inventories, down fifteen consecutive months, decreased $1.0 billion or 0.8 percent to $114.9
billion.

August 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars and exclude data for semiconductor manufacturing)

® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in August decreased $1.0 billion or 0.6 percent to $178.4 billion, the
Department of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed an 8.6 percent July increase. Excluding
transportation, new orders decreased 0.9 percent. Excluding defense, new orders increased 0.6 percent. Year to date, new orders
for 2002 were 1.2 percent below the same period a year ago.

Fabricated metal products had the largest decrease, $0.7 billion or 3.5 percent to $20.5 billion. Machinery, due to industrial
machinery manufacturing, decreased $0.6 billion or 2.5 percent to $22.5 billion.

® SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in August decreased $2.4 billion or 1.3 percent to $176.5 billion. This followed a
3.3 percent July increase. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 2.0 percent below the same period a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $1.8 billion or 3.3 percent to $53.1 billion, led by motor vehicles and parts
which decreased $0.9 billion and by nondefense aircraft and parts which also decreased by $0.9 billion.

e UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in August increased $1.9 billion or 0.4 percent to $490.9 billion. This
followed a 0.1 percent July increase.

Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $4.3 billion or 1.7 percent to $254.4 billion, due to nondefense aircraft and parts
which increased $3.5 billion. Fabricated metal products decreased $0.8 billion and machinery decreased $0.7 billion..

o INVENTORIES of manufactured durable goods in August, down nineteen consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 0.2
percent to $264.0 billion. This followed a 0.4 percent July decrease.

Computers and electronic products had the largest decrease, $0.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $42.8 billion, due to communications
equipment which decreased $0.2 billion. Machinery also decreased $0.2 billion or 0.4 percent to $44 .8 billion.

e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in August increased $1.6 billion or 28.9 percent to $7.1 billion.
Shipments increased 0.4 percent to $6.5 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.6 billion or 0.5 percent to $125.4 billion. Inventories
increased $0.5 billion or 2.7 percent to $18.5 billion.

e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in August increased $3.4 billion or 5.9 percent to $60.5
billion. Shipments decreased $1.0 billion or 1.7 percent to $57.4 billion. Unfilled orders increased $3.0 billion or 1.4 percent to

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS’ SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
December 2002
(Al figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars and exclude data for semiconductor manufacturing)
® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in December increased $0.4 billion or 0.2 percent to $170.1 billion, the Department of
Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 1.3 percent November decrease. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 1.1
percent. Excluding defense, new orders decreased 0.2 percent. New orders for 2002 were 0.1 percent below the prior year.
Computers and electronic products had the largest increase, $0.8 billion or 3.2 percent to $26.0 billion, due to computers and related products, which
increased by $0.8 billion. Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $0.9 billion or 1.9 percent to $49.5 billion, due to motor vehicles and
parts, which decreased by $1.6 billion.
© SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in December decreased $2.6 billion or 1.5 percent to $170.8 billion. This followed a 1.6 percent
November decrease. Shipments for 2002 were 0.6 percent below the prior year.
Transportation equipment, at the lowest level since September 2001, had the largest decrease, $2.3 billion or 4.4 percent to $49.0 billion, led by motor
vehicles and parts, which decreased by $1.5 billion.
¢ UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in December, down four consecutive months, decreased $0.7 billion or 0.2 percent to
$476.9 billion and were at the lowest level since September 1996. This followed a 0.8 percent November decrease.
Fabricated metal products had the largest decrease, $0.6 billion or 1.7 percent to $37.7 billion, the lowest level since February 1997. Machinery
decreased $0.3 billion or 0.7 percent to $44.7 billion, the lowest level since March 1994. Primary metals decreased $0.3 billion or 2.2 percent to
$14.9 billion, and was the lowest level since the current series began in 1992.
® INVENTORIES of manufactured durable goods in December increased $2.5 billion or 0.9 percent to $265.1 billion. This followed a 0.2 percent
November decrease and was the first increase since January 2001.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $2.7 billion or 3.9 percent to $72.9 billion, led by nondefense aircraft and parts, which increased by
$1.9 billion.
¢ CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in December increased $1.0 billion or 17.4 percent to $6.7 billion. Shipments
decreased $0.7 billion or 10.0 percent to $6.3 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $122.9 billion. Inventories increased
$0.5 billion or 2.7 percent to $19.0 billion.
o CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in December increased $1.5 billion or 2.8 percent to $56.0 billion. Shipments
decreased $0.6 billion or 1.1 percent to $55.5 billion. Unfilled orders increased $0.6 billion or 0.3 percent to $209.0 billion. Inventories increased
$0.9 billion or 0.8 percent to $112.6 billion, which was the first increase since January 2001.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
FEBRUARY 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in February increased $2.7 billion or 1.5 percent to $179.4 billion, the Department of
Commerce, Bureau of the Census reported today. This was the third consecutive increase and followed a 1.3 percent January increase.
Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 1.3 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 4.6 percent below the same period a year
ago.
Transportation equipment, led by aircraft and parts, had the largest increase, $4.4 billion or 8.6 percent to $55.3 billion; nondefense aircraft and
parts increased $2.2 billion or 47.2 percent to $7.0 billion. Electrical equipment increased $0.5 billion or 5.5 percent to $9.5 billion. Computers
and electronic products, down for the first time since September, decreased $0.8 billion or 2.4 percent to $33.6 billion.
® SHIPMENTS of durable goods in February decreased $5.9 billion or 3.2 percent to $178.0 billion. This followed a 1.8 percent January
increase. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 6.5 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment, down for the first time since September, had the largest decrease, $3.0 billion or 5.4 percent to $52.5 billion, mostly
due to motor vehicles and parts; nondefense aircraft and parts increased $0.1 billion or 2.0 percent to $7.7 billion. Computers and electronic
products, down for the first time since September, decreased $1.4 billion or 4.1 percent to $33.0 billion. Primary metals decreased $0.5 billion or
4.6 percent to $10.8 billion. Fabricated metal products decreased $0.4 billion or 2.2 percent to $19.8 billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS for durable goods in February increased $1.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $538.1 billion. This followed a 1.3 percent
January decrease.
Transportation equipment, led by ships and boats, had the largest increase, $2.8 billion or 1.0 percent to $274.9 billion; nondefense aircraft and
parts, down ten consecutive months, decreased $0.7 billion or 0.6 percent to $130.1 billion. Computers and electronic products increased $0.6
billion or 0.5 percent to $125.8 billion, due to semiconductors. Machinery, down seven of the last eight months, decreased $1.5 billion or 2.6
percent to $55.2 billion; this is the largest decrease on record.
® INVENTORIES for durable goods in February, down thirteen consecutive months, decreased $1.3 billion or 0.5 percent to $278.7 billion.
This followed a 0.9 percent January decrease.
Computers and electronic products, down twelve consecutive months, had the largest decrease, $0.5 billion or 1.0 percent to $48.4 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in February increased $3.7 billion or 78.6 percent to $8.5 billion. Shipments
decreased $0.6 billion or 9.0 percent to $6.4 billion. Unfilled orders increased $2.1 billion or 1.6 percent to $132.9 billion. Inventories
increased $0.2 billion or 0.8 percent to $18.8 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in February increased $2.7 billion or 4.9 percent to $57.3 billion.
Shipments decreased $0.5 billion or 0.8 percent to $59.4 billion. Unfilled orders, down fourteen consecutive months, decreased $2.0 billion or
0.9 percent to $238.3 billion. Inventories, down thirteen consecutive months, decreased $0.7 billion or 0.6 percent to $118.6 billion.
® REVISED JANUARY DATA Revised seasonally adjusted January figures for all manufacturing industries are: shipments, $331.3 billion
(revised from $333.2 billion); new orders, $324.1 billion (revised from $325.8 billion); unfilled orders, $536.7 billion (revised from $536.4
billion); and total inventories, $443.7 billion (revised from $444.4 billion).
