ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
July 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars and exclude data for semiconductor manufacturing)
® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in July increased $14.4 billion or 8.7 percent to $179.7 billion, the Department
of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 4.5 percent June decrease and is the largest increase since
October 2001. Excluding transportation, new orders increased 3.9 percent. Excluding Defense, new orders increased 7.3 percent;
this is the largest increase on record. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 1.9 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $9.8 billion or 20.8 percent to $56.7 billion, led mostly by aircraft and parts
which increased $6.9 billion. Machinery increased $2.5 billion or 11.8 percent to $23.3 billion; this is the largest increase on
record.
® SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in July increased $5.3 billion or 3.1 percent to $178.5 billion. This followed a 1.6
percent June decrease. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 2.4 percent below the same period a year ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $3.2 billion or 6.2 percent to $54.7 billion, led by motor vehicles and parts
which increased $2.8 billion. Computers and electronic products increased $0.9 billion or 3.5 percent to $27.0 billion.
¢ UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in July increased $1.3 billion or 0.3 percent to $489.8 billion. This
followed a 1.6 percent June decrease.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $2.0 billion or 0.8 percent to $249.9 billion, due to defense aircraft and parts
which increased $3.0 billion.
o INVENTORIES of manufactured durable goods in July, down eighteen consecutive months, decreased $1.0 billion or 0.4
percent to $264.5 billion. This followed a 0.3 percent June decrease.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $1.0 billion or 1.3 percent-to.$71.4 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in July decreased $0.9 billion or 14.3 percent to $5.4 billion.
Shipments decreased $0.2 billion or 3.2 percent to $6.5 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $1.1 billion or 0.9 percent to $124.7
billion. Inventories decreased $0.9 billion or 4.8 percent to $18.0 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in July increased $6.9 billion or 13.5 percent to $57.7
billion. Shipments increased $2.0 billion or 3.6 percent to $58.3 billion. Unfilled orders, down eighteen consecutive months,
decreased $0.7 billion or 0.3 percent to $213.6 billion. Inventories, down eighteen consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or
0.5 percent to $115.1 billion.

billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
March 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars)
® NEW ORDERS (excluding semiconductors) for manufactured durable goods in March decreased $1.0 billion or 0.6 percent to $173.4
billion, the Department of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 2.7 percent February increase. Excluding
transportation, new orders decreased 0.1 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 5.1 percent below the same period a year ago; new
orders for the first quarter were 0.6 percent above the fourth quarter.
Transportation equipment, mostly due to ships and boats, had the largest decrease, $0.9 billion or 1.6 percent to $55.9 billion; nondefense aircraft
and parts increased 0.3 percent to $7.8 billion. Machinery, down four consecutive months, decreased $0.3 billion or 1.4 percent to $21.8 billion.
® SHIPMENTS (excluding semiconductors) of durable goods in March slightly increased to $172.4 billion. This followed a 3.0 percent
February decrease. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 5.6 percent below the same period a year ago; shipments for the first quarter were
slightly above the fourth quarter.
Primary metals had the largest increase, $0.4 billion or 3.8 percent to $11.3 billion. Machinery decreased $0.4 billion or 1.8 percent to $23.1
billion, due to turbine and generators. Transportation equipment also decreased $0.4 billion or 0.7 percent to $52.4 billion, due to motor vehicles
and parts; nondefense aircraft and parts increased 0.4 percent to $8.1 billion.
® UNFILLED ORDERS (excluding semiconductors) for durable goods in March increased $1.0 billion or 0.2 percent to $524.5 billion.
This followed a 0.4 percent February increase.
Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $3.5 billion or 1.3 percent to $279.8 billion; nondefense aircraft and parts, down eleven
consecutive months, decreased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $130.1 billion. Machinery, down eight of the last nine months, decreased $1.3
billion or 2.3 percent to $54.0 billion.
® INVENTORIES (excluding semiconductors) for durable goods in March, down fourteen consecutive months, decreased $2.9 billion or
1.1 percent to $268.2 billion. This followed a 0.7 percent February decrease.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $2.0 billion or 2.7 percent to $71.1 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in March increased $1.5 billion or 17.8 percent to $10.2 billion. Shipments
increased $0.5 billion or 8.6 percent to $6.9 billion. Unfilled orders increased $3.3 billion or 2.5 percent to $136.2 billion. Inventories
decreased $0.1 billion or 0.5 percent to $18.7 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in March decreased $1.6 billion or 2.8 percent to $55.7 billion.
Shipments increased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to $59.2 billion. Unfilled orders, down fifteen consecutive months, decreased $3.5 billion or 1.5
percent to $235.3 billion. Inventories, down fourteen consecutive months, decreased $2.1 billion or 1.8 percent to $116.1 billion.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $1.1 billion or 2.0 percent to $52.5 billion, led by motor vehicles and parts.

® UNFILLED ORDERS, excluding semiconductors, for durable goods in May decreased $2.9 billion or 0.6 percent to $496.4 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
November 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars and exclude data for semiconductor manufacturing)

® NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in November decreased $2.3 billion or 1.4 percent to $169.6 billion, the
Department of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 1.7 percent October increase. Excluding
transportation, new orders decreased 1.3 percent. Excluding defense, new orders decreased 2.3 percent. Year to date, new orders for
2002 were 0.2 percent below the same period a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $0.8 billion or 1.6 percent to $49.4 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts, which
decreased by $1.7 billion. Machinery decreased $0.7 billion or 3.2 percent to $21.9 billion. Primary metals decreased $0.5 billion or
4.6 percent to $10.7 billion, which was the largest decrease since October 2000.

e SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in November decreased $2.2 billion or 1.3 percent to $174.2 billion. This followed a
1.4 percent October increase. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 0.6 percent below the same period a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $1.9 billion or 3.5 percent to $51.8 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts, which
decreased by $2.0 billion.

® UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in November, down three consecutive months, decreased $4.5 billion or 0.9
percent to $476.8 billion and were at the lowest level since September 1996. This followed a 0.9 percent October decrease.
Transportation equipment, at the lowest level since May 2000, had the largest decrease, $2.4 billion or 1.0 percent to $246.0 billion, led
by nondefense aircraft and parts, which decreased $1.7 billion.

® INVENTORIES of manufactured durable goods in November, down twenty-two consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 0.2
percent to $262.6 billion and were at the lowest level since November 1995. This followed a 0.2 percent October decrease.
Transportation equipment, at the lowest level since December 1997, had the largest decrease, $0.7 billion or 1.0 percent to $70.2
billion.

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in November increased $1.2 billion or 28.6 percent to $5.5 billion.
Shipments increased $0.4 billion or 6.2 percent to $7.0 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $1.5 billion or 1.2 percent to $122.4 billion.
Inventories increased 0.3 percent to $18.5 billion.

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in November decreased $1.8 billion or 3.2 percent to $53.6
billion. Shipments decreased $0.8 billion or 1.3 percent to $56.5 billion. Unfilled orders, down twenty-one of the last twenty-two
months, decreased $2.9 billion or 1.4 percent to $207.1 billion, the lowest level since January 1996. Inventories, down twenty-two
consecutive months, decreased $0.4 billion or 0.3 percent to $111.7 billion, the lowest level since December 1995.

¢ NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in October increased $4.8 billion or 2.8 percent to $173.9 billion, the Department

orders increased 2.4 percent. Excluding defense, new orders increased 3.8 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 0.5 percent
below the same period a year ago.

Transportation equipment had the largest increase, $2.0 billion or 4.0 percent to $51.3 billion, led by motor vehicles and parts which

communications equipment. The communications equipment increase of $2.0 billion was the largest increase since January 1997.

® SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in October increased $2.1 billion or 1.2 percent to $176.1 billion. This followed a 0.9

increased by $1.6 billion.

® UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in October decreased $2.2 billion or 0.5 percent to $483.6 billion and were
at the lowest level since October 1996. This followed a 1.0 percent September decrease.

Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $2.4 billion or 1.0 percent to $249.5 billion, due to nondefense aircraft and parts,

® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in October decreased $1.3 billion or 17.2 percent to $6.2 billion.

ADVANCE REPORT ON DURABLE GOODS MANUFACTURERS' SHIPMENTS, INVENTORIES, AND ORDERS
September 2002
(All figures in text below are in seasonally adjusted current dollars and exclude data for semiconductor manufacturing)
e NEW ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in September decreased $10.5 billion or 5.9 percent to $167.6 billion, the
Department of Commerce, U.S. Census Bureau reported today. This followed a 0.6 percent August decrease and was the largest
decrease since November 2001 which also had a 5.9 percent decrease. Excluding transportation, new orders decreased 1.0 percent.
Excluding defense, new orders decreased 6.0 percent. Year to date, new orders for 2002 were 0.6 percent below the same period a year
ago.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $9.3 billion or 16.1 percent to $48.4 billion and was the largest decrease since
November 2001, led by nondefense aircraft and parts which decreased by $4.2 billion.
® SHIPMENTS of manufactured durable goods in September decreased $1.9 billion or 1.1 percent to $173.9 billion. This followed a
1.6 percent August decrease. Year to date, shipments for 2002 were 1.4 percent below the same period a year ago. :
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $0.6 billion or 1.2 percent to $52.2 billion, due to motor vehicles and parts which
decreased $1.4 billion.
@ UNFILLED ORDERS for manufactured durable goods in September decreased $6.3 billion or 1.3 percent to $485.0 billion. This
followed a 0.5 percent August increase and was at the lowest level since October 1996.
Transportation equipment had the largest decrease, $3.8 billion or 1.5 percent to $251.3 billion, due to nondefense aircraft and parts
which decreased $1.5 billion. Computers and electronic products, down twenty consecutive months, decreased $2.1 billion or 1.9
percent to $108.7 billion, due to communications equipment which decreased $2.8 billion.
e INVENTORIES of manufactured durable goods in September, down twenty consecutive months, decreased $0.5 billion or 0.2
percent to $263.5 billion. This followed a 0.2 percent August decrease and was at the lowest level since December 1995.
Transportation equipment, down six of the last seven months and at the lowest level since January 1998, had the largest decrease, $0.3
billion or 0.4 percent to $70.8 billion, due to nondefense aircraft and parts which decreased $0.8 billion.
® CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, DEFENSE New orders in September decreased $0.3 billion or 4.1 percent to $6.7 billion.
Shipments increased $0.3 billion or 4.3 percent to $6.8 billion. Unfilled orders decreased $0.1 billion or 0.1 percent to $125.2 billion.
Inventories decreased $0.1 billion or 0.3 percent to $18.5 billion.
e CAPITAL GOODS INDUSTRIES, NONDEFENSE New orders in September decreased $7.5 billion or 12.6 percent to $52.1
billion, the largest decrease since December 1997. Shipments decreased $0.4 billion or 0.6 percent to $56.6 billion. Unfilled orders,
down nineteen of the last twenty months and at the lowest level since April 1996, decreased $4.5 billion or 2.1 percent to $211.0 billion.
Inventories, down twenty consecutive months and at the lowest level since June 1996, decreased $0.8 billion or 0.7 percent to $113.2
billion.
® REVISED AUGUST DATA Revised seasonally adjusted August figures for all manufacturing industries are: new orders, $325.5
billion (revised from $326.6 billion); shipments, $323.2 billion (revised from $324.2 billion); unfilled orders, $491.3 billion (revised
from $491.4 billion); and total inventories, $428.2 billion (revised from $427.9 billion).
